:::{#exm-derivative}
#### The derivative of $x^2$

For $f(x) = x^2$,
the computation in @exm-differentiable, with $3$ replaced by any real number $c$,
gives $\frac{f(c + h) - f(c)}{h} = 2c + h$, which tends to $2c$ as $h \to 0$.
So the derivative of $f$ is $f'(x) = 2x$.
For example, $f'(3) = 6$ and $f'(-1) = -2$.

:::
